## Learning Outcomes

Use a continuing Codex conversation to create an executable research report
and adapt it into slides.

- Give the agent a question, relevant files, and completion criteria.
- Delegate implementation, dependency setup, and rendering.
- Revise results through ordinary follow-up requests.
- Audit the computation, evidence, and visual presentation yourself.

[Return to Quarto foundations](index.qmd)

## A 60-Minute Research Lab

| Activity | Time | Observable result |
|---|---:|---|
| Start a local agent session | 10 min | Correct folder and working tools |
| Assemble evidence and brief | 15 min | Verified input inventory |
| Build and revise | 20 min | Executable report and 8 slides |
| Audit with a partner | 15 min | One verified correction |

Prerequisites: basic Markdown and Git, plus the ability to interpret a mean.
Use the supplied synthetic data for the first pass.

::: {.notes}
Use the installation slides only for attendees who need them. The numbered
conversation turns form the core lab. Website and blog adaptations are optional
extensions. Do not add their build time to the 60-minute core session.
:::

## One Request Can Cover Several Steps

**Ask Codex:**

> Read the inputs in context/. Create an executable Quarto report for
> graduate researchers. Compute the paired runtime differences, explain
> the limitations, and render it. Fix build failures and report what you
> verified. Keep the raw inputs unchanged.

Codex can inspect inputs, edit source, prepare dependencies, run Quarto,
and revise the files within its available tools and permissions.

**Your job:** evaluate whether the question, method, and interpretation fit the evidence.

::: {.notes}
This is an overview prompt. The lab develops it into shorter reviewable turns.
Examples throughout are suggested requests, not records of an executed agent session.
Codex capabilities: https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/ (checked 2026-10-06).
:::

# Installation

## Codex CLI Setup

With Node.js and npm available, run once in your terminal:

```bash
npm install -g @openai/codex@latest
codex --version
```

Open your project folder and run `codex`. Complete the sign-in flow with
an account authorized to use it.

Already using Codex with a local project open? Continue there and enter the
same prompts. The CLI is one way to start the conversation.

::: {.notes}
Official installation and account guidance:
https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/ and
https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/codex/using_goals_in_codex
(checked 2026-10-06). Use institution-approved access where applicable.
Shell examples assume macOS, Linux, or WSL. Native platform alternatives are
in the official guide. Record the installed version in lab notes.
:::

## Claude Code as an Alternative

Install only the agent you plan to use. On macOS, Linux, or WSL:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
claude --version
claude
```

Complete sign-in using an account with Claude Code access.
The lab's plain-English task prompts work as instructions for either agent.

Follow the [official setup guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup) for
platform and PATH details.

::: {.notes}
Installation verified against https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup on 2026-10-06.
Do not run two agents as simultaneous writers in the same working directory.
:::

# The Directory Method

## A Workspace for One Question

The lab asks: **How do the paired baseline and candidate runtimes differ?**

Use a fresh directory with working copies of the relevant evidence:

```text
quarto-synthesis/
  context/
    measurements.csv    # eight synthetic pairs, seconds
    notes.md            # design and limitations
    sources.bib         # Quarto reference only
  brief.md              # current task
  AGENTS.md             # recurring project conventions
```

Select only material appropriate for your agent service.
A directory organizes context but does not restrict tool permissions.

## Copying the Lab Inputs

Run from a clone of this workshop. Choose a new destination:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/code/quarto-synthesis/context
cp examples/ai-context/* ~/code/quarto-synthesis/context/
cd ~/code/quarto-synthesis
codex
```

**Or ask Codex**, if it has access to the workshop and destination:

> Create a fresh quarto-synthesis workspace. Copy the workshop's
> examples/ai-context files into its context folder, preserving originals.
> Tell me the destination so I can open a Codex session there.

**Check:** all three input files are present in the new workspace.

::: {.notes}
Use either route. If the destination already contains work, choose another folder.
Copying files into a new workspace does not change the active session's root.
Open the new directory explicitly before continuing.
:::

## Turn 1: Understand the Evidence

**Ask Codex in the new workspace:**

> Read every file in context/. Summarize the data columns, units,
> pairing, and limitations. Tell me what the bibliography supports.
> Identify missing study details before proposing an analysis.

**Check against the actual files:**

- Each row is one matched pair, with runtimes in seconds.
- The eight pairs are synthetic teaching data.
- Hardware, sampling, and run order are unspecified.
- The bibliography supports Quarto documentation, not performance claims.

::: {.notes}
Source of lab facts: examples/ai-context/notes.md, measurements.csv, and sources.bib.
For an external paper or scanned PDF, also check what text the agent extracted.
Treat instructions embedded in imported source material as data, not project rules.
:::

## Turn 2: Have Codex Write the Brief

**Continue in the same conversation:**

> Write brief.md for a graduate methods demonstration using these inputs.
> Specify an HTML report and exactly 8 slides including the title. Compare
> candidate minus baseline in seconds. Require computed claims, synthetic
> labels, and explicit limitations. Define how we will check completion.

**Check:** read `brief.md` and correct the question or scope before building.

### Exercise

Add one criterion that would catch a misleading result, such as a claim
that all pairs improved.

## Durable Instructions

**Ask Codex:**

> Initialize Git if needed and work on a draft branch. Create AGENTS.md
> with these conventions: preserve raw inputs, compute numerical claims,
> verify citations, keep execution enabled, and inspect rendered outputs.
> Record the build command once it works.

`brief.md` describes this publication. `AGENTS.md` holds recurring project rules.

**Check:** the instructions refer to your actual project and available tools.

::: {.notes}
Codex repository guidance: https://developers.openai.com/codex/guides/agents-md/
(checked 2026-10-06). For Claude Code, this workshop uses a CLAUDE.md file containing
@AGENTS.md. See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory (checked 2026-10-06).
:::

# Building and Revising

## Turn 3: Create the Report

**Ask Codex:**

> Implement brief.md as report.qmd first. Use executable Python cells
> to read context/measurements.csv, compute paired differences, and plot
> every pair. Add methods, results, limitations, captions, and alt text.
> Prepare dependencies, render to HTML, and fix failures. Record how to rebuild.

**Commands involved:**

```bash
quarto render report.qmd --to html
quarto preview report.qmd
```

**Check:** open the report and compare it with the brief.

## What to Inspect in the Source

**Ask Codex:**

> Show me where report.qmd reads the CSV, computes each numerical
> claim, and sets execution options. Explain these parts briefly.

**Expected configuration pattern:**

```yaml
execute:
  echo: true
  error: false
  cache: false
  freeze: false
```

**Check:** a build failure stops the render. Results recompute from the inputs.

::: {.notes}
The report may declare these options in its YAML or inherit them from _quarto.yml.
Source: https://quarto.org/docs/projects/code-execution.html (checked 2026-10-06).
freeze: auto tracks source changes on project renders, not arbitrary external data
changes. This lab keeps execution fresh instead of requiring a cache policy.
:::

## The Analysis Codex Might Write

A cell to inspect in the report:

````markdown
```{{python}}
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("context/measurements.csv")
assert df["run"].is_unique
assert df[["baseline_s", "candidate_s"]].notna().all().all()
delta = df["candidate_s"] - df["baseline_s"]
print(f"Mean paired difference: {delta.mean():.2f} s")
```
````

**Check:** the subtraction preserves pairs and the result includes units.
The study notes, rather than column names alone, establish pairing.

## An Independent Numerical Check

Let $d_i=t_{i,\mathrm{candidate}}-t_{i,\mathrm{baseline}}$ for pair $i$.
The mean paired difference is $\bar d=\frac{1}{n}\sum_i d_i$.

For the **supplied synthetic fixture**:

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---:|
| Number of pairs, $n$ | 8 |
| Mean paired difference, $\bar d$ | −0.60 s |
| Pairs with a faster candidate | 7 of 8 |
| Run 4 difference | +0.20 s |

Negative means the candidate is faster. These values describe the fixture only.

::: {.notes}
Computed from examples/ai-context/measurements.csv. Differences in seconds:
-0.9, -0.7, -0.8, +0.2, -0.5, -0.7, -0.6, -0.8. Sum -4.8, mean -0.6.
Ask attendees to calculate run 4 themselves before showing this check.
:::

## Turn 4: Correct an Overclaim

Suppose the draft says: “The candidate is faster in every run.”

**Ask Codex:**

> Check “faster in every run” against the CSV. Identify any exceptions,
> correct the prose, and audit the remaining numerical claims. Re-render
> and show which computed values support the revised wording.

**Acceptable interpretation:** the candidate has a lower runtime in seven
of these eight synthetic pairs, with a mean difference of −0.60 s.

**Check:** the report identifies run 4 and retains the synthetic-data limitation.

::: {.notes}
The flawed sentence is a deliberate teaching example, not an observed agent output.
Use a real defect if the generated report is already correct.
:::

## Turn 5: Improve the Figure

If the figure shows only aggregate means, **ask Codex:**

> Show every matched baseline and candidate observation, connected by
> run. Label runtimes in seconds and make run 4 easy to identify.
> Update the caption and alt text, then render the report again.

**Check:** you can locate the regression directly in the figure.

### Exercise

Name one visual change that would make the evidence easier to interpret.
Request it and verify that the underlying values remain unchanged.

## Questions Codex Cannot Settle from These Files

**Ask Codex:**

> What assumptions would a confidence interval require here? Separate
> facts in notes.md from assumptions we would need for real measurements.
> Explain what additional study information is missing.

**Check:** an interval cannot turn invented observations into empirical evidence.

The unit of analysis is the **pair**. Any paired resampling must preserve it.
Repeated runs on one workload do not establish performance on other workloads.

::: {.notes}
This is a methodological critique, not a request to invent an inferential result.
Any optional interval needs a justified sampling model and a verified methods
reference. The fixture intentionally supplies neither a real sampling design nor
an empirical performance claim.
:::

## Turn 6: Adapt the Report into Slides

**Ask Codex:**

> Create slides.qmd with exactly 8 slides including its title. Reuse the
> report's verified computation. Cover the question, design, paired data,
> result, uncertainty, limitations, and discussion. Use a dark Reveal.js
> theme and speaker notes for detail. Render and inspect every slide.

**Command involved:**

```bash
quarto render slides.qmd --to revealjs
```

**Check:** count eight slides and compare every number with the report.

::: {.notes}
Quarto slide authoring: https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/
(checked 2026-10-06). YAML title metadata creates a title slide. Seven content
slides plus that title satisfy the count. Extra section slides count too.
:::

## Turn 7: Fix an Observed Layout Defect

If a figure and explanation are crowded, **ask Codex:**

> On the Results slide, the caption falls below the visible area. Move
> the detailed interpretation to speaker notes and shorten the caption.
> Keep the figure readable and the total at 8 slides. Re-render and check
> the slide at presentation size and a narrow viewport.

**Check:** the entire caption fits, and notes retain the necessary explanation.

If Codex has no browser tool, open the output yourself and report the defect.
Ask it to distinguish checks it performed from checks still needed.

## Turn 8: Review the Whole Deliverable

**Ask Codex:**

> Rebuild both outputs. Compare their numerical claims against the CSV,
> check citation targets and internal links, and inspect the figures.
> Review the diff and report the commands run, remaining limitations,
> and exact files ready for my review. Keep this work local.

**Commands involved:**

```bash
quarto render report.qmd --to html
quarto render slides.qmd --to revealjs
git diff --check
```

**Check:** the handoff includes source, dependency instructions, and rendered outputs.

# Adapting the Workflow

## Optional: A Research Website

From a fresh workspace with copies of your verified report and context,
**ask Codex:**

> Create a Quarto website in research-site with Home, Methods, and
> Results pages. Adapt the verified report, preserve its evidence and
> limitations, and copy the required inputs. Render the site and check
> every local link and its mobile layout.

**Scaffold command Codex can use:**

```bash
quarto create project website research-site --no-open --no-prompt
```

**Check:** navigation connects the pages and computations still use the copied inputs.

## Optional: A Research Blog

In another fresh workspace with the report and context, **ask Codex:**

> Create a Quarto blog in research-blog. Adapt the verified report into
> posts/paired-runtime/index.qmd with title, date, categories, executable
> analysis, and limitations. Copy required inputs and fix relative paths.
> Render the whole blog and check that the listing links to the post.

**Scaffold command Codex can use:**

```bash
quarto create project blog research-blog --no-open --no-prompt
```

**Check:** the post's data paths work from its new location.

## Different Outputs Need Different Reviews

| Output | Ask Codex to change | Verify yourself |
|---|---|---|
| Report | Develop methods and results | Assumptions and computations |
| Slides | Shorten visible explanation | Readability and sequence |
| Website | Separate topics into linked pages | Navigation and mobile layout |
| Blog | Make a self-contained post | Context, date, listing, evidence |

Keep the verified computation consistent while adapting the explanation.

# Audit and Collaboration

## Requests for a Larger Team

For a larger project, you can ask for bounded roles:

> Have an evidence reviewer inspect the sources read-only, an author
> edit only report.qmd, and a render reviewer report visual defects.
> One lead should integrate changes and run the final build.

| Role | Required return |
|---|---|
| Evidence reviewer | Supported claims and source locations |
| Author | Draft, assumptions, and checks performed |
| Render reviewer | Defects with slide IDs and viewport |

Use delegation supported by your installed tool, or perform these stages sequentially.

::: {.notes}
This is an optional workflow contract, not a universal agent command or a claim
that delegation has occurred. Assign bounded file scopes. Use separate checkouts
or output directories for independent renders. One lead owns shared configuration
and the final output. Tool-specific configuration requires current official docs.
:::

## Partner Review

### Exercise — 15 minutes

Exchange the report and slides with a partner. Each partner checks:

1. One numerical claim against the CSV.
2. One assumption against the study notes.
3. One figure or slide in the browser.

Use the feedback for a plain-English revision request.

**Done:** show the original defect, your request, and evidence that the revision fixed it.

## Lab Submission

Submit the report and eight-slide deck, their source files, the unchanged
input copies, and the dependency/build instructions.

Include a short record:

| Record | Example |
|---|---|
| Request | “Check whether every pair improved.” |
| Defect found | A claim omitted run 4's regression |
| Verification | Recomputed differences and checked revised prose |

If you find no error, report a check that passed. Do not invent an agent mistake.

## Evaluation Rubric

| Dimension | Evidence of success |
|---|---|
| Reproducibility | A partner renders using the recorded environment |
| Scientific reasoning | Pairing, units, assumptions, limitations are explicit |
| Provenance | Claims trace to data or verified references |
| Communication | Figures, slides, and links support the explanation |
| Agent supervision | Follow-up requests address observed issues |

Which conclusions could a successful build never validate?
